title: FDR/statistics validation harness
context: Target-decoy FDR control is the foundational statistical safeguard in proteomics: if FDR is misconfigured (wrong decoy strategy, wrong threshold, wrong level — PSM/peptide/protein), the published protein list is inflated or deflated in ways that invalidate the entire reanalysis. The FDR/statistics validation harness checks that FDR is actually controlled at the documented level on each run, not just configured, and validates downstream statistical models (e.g., MSstats/limma settings). This must be a CI gate, not a post-hoc check.
objective: Implement an FDR and statistics validation harness that runs as a CI gate, verifying that target-decoy FDR is controlled at the documented level and that downstream statistical parameters match the pinned model specification.
acceptanceCriteria: The harness checks that target-decoy FDR is controlled at the documented level (typically 1%) at the PSM, peptide, and protein levels on each pipeline run, using the decoy method and thresholds recorded in the run manifest.
The harness validates that downstream statistical analysis parameters (e.g., MSstats/limma settings) match the pinned, documented model and that no undeclared parameters are used.
The CI gate fails the build if FDR control cannot be verified or if statistical parameters diverge from the pinned model.
Golden fixtures use synthetic or tiny public spectra only (no patient-derived raw data).
pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint pass; code is MIT-licensed; commit is DCO signed-off.
resources: PLAN.md — Pipeline stages (FDR & statistics section), Tech stack
output: A committed FDR and statistics validation harness integrated as a CI gate with synthetic golden fixtures and passing pnpm build/test/lint; MIT-licensed.
